text:
ConocoPhillips rose 1.6% today, continuing a rebound that's gained 4% over the past four trading days after dropping 7.6% in the prior two weeks. The bounce reflects stabilization in oil prices—US crude is holding around $89.60 per barrel—combined with what appears to be renewed investor interest, flagged by CNBC's "Calls of the day" segment on November 11th, which highlighted the stock as a notable pick.

The earlier sell-off likely reflects supply concerns that have now eased: the IEA reported on November 13th that Russian crude production rebounded to 8.73 million barrels per day in October, pushing global oil markets back into surplus after a period of tighter supply. That shift away from supply-constrained markets had weighed on energy stocks, but the stabilization since then has allowed buyers to step back in.
